key_insight: Optical-fiber daylighting can cut vertical-farm lighting electricity use substantially, but current fiber costs keep it from being economically competitive with rooftop PV.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows how daylight distribution, spectral filtering, and hybrid LED-daylight control can reshape vertical-farm energy performance without sacrificing all crop output.
method: Validated transient vertical-farm model linked to Tonatiuh ray tracing
Compared 5 optical-fiber types and 3 daylighting strategies
Benchmarked against light-pipe and rooftop photovoltaic options
evidence_signal: The study reports 19–27% useful-PAR delivery efficiency for optical fibers, up to 89% electricity reduction in some configurations, and an 11–12-year payback for rooftop PV.
watch_item: Economic viability is limited by high optical-fiber capital cost, with the authors estimating about a 90% cost reduction would be needed for competitiveness.
paper_title: Can sunlight replace LEDs in vertical farms? A critical assessment of optical-fiber daylighting strategies
